title: Letter analysis result
description: What /v1/analyze returns for one photographed letter. Used verbatim as the model's structured-output schema. Enum members are injected at boot from contracts/catalogue.json — see the $comment on each field for which path supplies them. The schema is never hand-edited to add a key; add it to index.html and regenerate the catalogue.

agency.$comment: enum := Object.keys(catalogue.agencies). null when the letter names no agency this app knows.

agency_child.$comment: One of catalogue.agencies[agency].children, when the parent is an umbrella (bank, health fund).
agency_child.description: The specific bank or health fund, when the agency is an umbrella entry.

template.$comment: enum := Object.keys(catalogue.templates). null when the letter is about no known process.
template.description: Which known process this letter belongs to, if any.

evidence.description: The Hebrew phrase in the letter that asks for this document. Quoted, not paraphrased — it is what the user checks the suggestion against.

required_docs.description: Documents the letter asks for, as catalogue keys. Each already carries four translations and a Hebrew term, so no name is ever generated.

he.description: Hebrew name exactly as the letter writes it. Not translated — the client shows it verbatim and labels it unverified.

extra_docs.description: Requested documents with no catalogue key. Surfaced separately and never silently mixed into required_docs, because these are the ones that can be wrong.

deadline.$comment: ISO 8601 date. The model resolves relative wording ('תוך 30 יום') against letter_date, and returns null rather than guessing when letter_date is unreadable.

letter_date.description: The date printed on the letter, needed to resolve relative deadlines.

reference.description: The אסמכתא / case number, copied character for character. This is the thing worth arguing with later.

form_code.description: The form or letter code printed on the page — 'בל/250', 'טופס 101', a departmental letter number. Israeli agency correspondence almost always carries one, and it is the cheapest reliable way to recognise a letter as one we have seen before.
form_code.$comment: Impersonal by construction: it identifies the template, not the recipient. The server hashes it with the agency and normalised title into a form_signature, and that signature is the only thing that may be stored.

form_title_he.description: The letter's own heading in Hebrew, verbatim. Second input to the signature, for letters that carry no code.

personalised.description: True when the letter is individual correspondence — a caseworker writing about one person's specific situation — rather than a standard template. A personalised letter is never promoted to the shared catalogue, whatever its signature.

confidence.description: Overall. Below the server threshold the result is returned but the client adds nothing.

language.description: Language the letter is written in. At launch anything but 'he' is returned with a low confidence and no additions.

not_a_letter.description: The image is not an agency letter — a selfie, a receipt, a blurry frame. Set by the Haiku pre-check without reaching the main model.
